newsitem.title: USA: Quantum says turnaround is on track.
newsitem.headline: Quantum says turnaround is on track.

text.p: Quantum Corp said on Monday its second quarter financial performance shows the company is on track to boost its top of the line computer disk drive recording head businesses.
Earlier, Quantum reported a profit of $0.08 a share on sales of $1.12 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 1997 versus a profit of $0.39 per primary share on sales of $1.03 billion, one year ago.
"Although below our potential, our results this quarter reflect performance that is on target for our turnaround," Michael Brown, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"Nine months ago, we embarked on a strategy to bring our high-end disk drive and recording heads businesses to a break-even position by the end of our fiscal year," added Brown, "We must execute well over the next two quarters, but we have accomplished what we expected thus far."
In the second quarter, shipments of desktop-class hard disk drives were basically flat with the June quarter as the company executed a significant product transition.
Sales of Quantum's DLT tape products increased to $150 million for the quarter, were up 20 percent from the June quarter and nearly twice what they were a year ago.

In October, Quantum began production shipments of 2.2, 4.5, and 9.1 gigabyte Atlas II drives, the first high-end drives to be built by Quantum's manufacturing partner, Matsushita-Kotobuki Electronics.
The Atlas II products are in qualification with virtually all the major high-end system manufacturers, Quantum said.
